messages:
Maya Patel: :rotating_light: noticing a p95/p99 spike on streaming endpoints in us-west-2 starting ~T-5m. p95 ~1.1s -> 2.3s, p99 ~1.8s -> 4.2s. Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream and /v1/generate/stream. Pretty broad across multiple model shards.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-5712348901 - KV cache pressure causing streaming tail latency. Pager duty notified. Severity: P1 (potential customer impact).

oncall-pager: paging Devin Ortiz (on-call SRE).

Devin Ortiz: I’m on it. Maya, any error spikes or increased 5xx?

Maya Patel: 5xx rate small uptick (~0.2%) but not huge. Most requests succeed but take much longer. Streaming stall symptoms: clients not receiving tokens for several seconds. Logs show lots of `KV_EVICT` events and prefill queue growth.

Samir Khan: Adding what I see from infra metrics: KV cache hit rate dropped from 94% -> 68% on several shards. Eviction rate spiked. Memory fragmentation metrics show slab utilization uneven: shard-12 and shard-19 at 82% free vs shard-7 at 18% free. Looks like hot/cold fragmentation after recent rollout.

Maya Patel: Posting a sample from the stream node logs (decoding module):

```
2026-03-15T12:03:22Z decoder-7 WARN prefill_queue_len=237 decode_queue_len=12 kv_evict=1.4/s
2026-03-15T12:03:23Z kv-shard-7 INFO evicting 12 pages cause=slab_pressure fragment_pct=41
2026-03-15T12:03:24Z stream-proxy WARN stall_detected duration=3.4s route=/v1/chat/stream
```

Maya Patel: The interesting bit — prefill tasks are queuing up much more than decode tasks; prefill workers are far busier and appear to be triggering eviction churn. I think a prefetch/prefill vs decode imbalance is thrashing the cache.

Devin Ortiz: Hypothesis: recent rollout to add eager prefetch of KV pages for long-context requests increased prefill pressure, and combined with skewed shard allocation now causing evictions on a subset of shards. That yields more page faults on decode which stall streaming while prefill re-populates.

Samir Khan: Agree. Observed that requests with long prefixes (>=1024 tokens) trigger prefetch across multiple shards. Prefetch concurrency recently bumped in the runtime config `runtime.prefill_concurrency=12` (rollout last night).

Maya Patel: Customer impact: Lina from CS — any inbound tickets?

Lina (Customer Success): Yes, two enterprise tenants reported degraded streaming responsiveness and user-perceived stalls starting ~12:03 PDT. Both onshore customers; one is seeing intermittent session timeouts from their app (they are retrying and getting higher overall latency).

Devin Ortiz: Immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back `runtime.prefill_concurrency` to previous value, 2) throttle/disable eager prefetch for high-length requests, 3) isolate heavily-fragmented shards (drain new allocations away), 4) emergency mem-compact/defrag on affected hosts (risky). Prefer non-disruptive first.

Maya Patel: Can we apply a targeted throttling rule: if request.prefix_len > 800 AND route=stream then set `prefill=false` (fall back to on-demand decode)? That would reduce prefill churn for long streams without full rollback.

Devin Ortiz: Good idea. I can push a runtime patch to gate prefill behind a request-based predicate. Patching config and hot-reload in 2-3min.

Samir Khan: Also recommend reducing `runtime.prefill_concurrency` from 12 -> 6 as a low-risk change while we validate the predicate. I'll prepare the change but hold till Devin signals go-ahead.

incident-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction-wave - recommended mitigations listed.

Devin Ortiz: Rolling predicate now to us-west-2 stream-proxies (canary on 10% traffic). Patch command: `kubectl set env ds/stream-proxy RUNTIME_PREFILL_PREDICATE='prefix_len<=800' --namespace=runtime`

Maya Patel: Canary traffic looks cleaner already; p95 down ~20% on canary subset. No new 5xxs.

Devin Ortiz: Scaling predicate to 50% while Samir prepares concurrency change.

Samir Khan: Prepared config diff for `runtime.prefill_concurrency` but holding. Also spinning up an extra cache shard pool to move a few hot partitions off shard-7. `cachectl rebalance --move partition 7->20,21` (taking ~30s per partition).

Maya Patel: Observability notes: add a heatmap for eviction-by-partition and correlate prefill queue length vs streaming-stall rate. I'll open a quick dashboard so we can watch.

Lina (Customer Success): Please keep us posted on ETA for Affected tenants. I have a support channel open with customer engineers. They want a mitigation ETA and notes to send to product teams.

Devin Ortiz: Current status: predicate rolled to 50%; p99 for stream routes in us-west-2 from 4.2s -> 2.1s on canary group, global p99 trending down. Continuing rollout to 100% — will pause if error rate increases.

Maya Patel: After predicate at 100%: global p99 now ~1.9s, p95 ~1.1s. Eviction rate reduced by ~65%. Prefill queue length normalized.

Samir Khan: Initiating shard rebalance to relieve fragment hotspots. Moving partitions one-by-one. Expect full rebalance ~25-30m.

Devin Ortiz: For post-incident follow-up: capture timeline, correlate with last-night rollout that changed `prefill_concurrency`, verify canary coverage gap, add a gating test for prefill pressure in our CI, and consider adaptive prefill throttling by shard health.

Maya Patel: Lina, for customers: suggest messaging that we mitigated the immediate latency by disabling eager prefill for very long streams and are performing a shard rebalance to permanently reduce eviction churn. We'll follow with a detailed RCA.

Lina (Customer Success): Copy. I'll send an interim update to the impacted tenants now. Thanks. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-5712348901 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Please file a postmortem within 72 hours.

Devin Ortiz: Handing off to Samir for the longer-running rebalance and follow-up RCA. Samir — you own the postmortem.

Samir Khan: Got it. I'll keep monitoring; will post progress updates here as partitions move and memory fragmentation improves.

Maya Patel: Thanks team. Closing live triage channel; will update thread with any regressions.

(oncall-pager reacts with :thumbsup:)
